conversation.content:
Hello, I’m Dr. Martinez, a perinatal mental-health clinician. I’m here to make sure you’re getting the emotional support you deserve after having your baby.

Today I’d like to do a quick check-in using the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale—usually just called the EPDS. It’s a 10-question screening that helps us understand how you’ve been feeling emotionally over the past seven days. It’s completely confidential, and there are no right or wrong answers; we simply want to hear your honest experience so we can offer the right support if you need it.

We’ll go through each question one at a time. If any question feels difficult, we can pause or reword it so it feels manageable. Ready to begin?

First, in the past week, how often have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things?

Hmm… most days I still can laugh a little—like if my partner does something silly or the baby makes a funny face—but it feels harder than it used to. I’d say I still find things amusing, just not quite as easily. Maybe some days yes, some days not really.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things
Most of the time I can still laugh, but it takes more effort than before the baby. Some days yes, some days not really.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

I still look forward to little things—like taking the baby for a walk or having my morning coffee—but the excitement isn’t as strong as it used to be. It feels more like “I guess that’ll be nice” rather than really looking forward to it.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yeah… I catch myself doing that. Like if the baby’s fussy and I can’t settle him right away, I start thinking maybe I’m just not doing something right or I’m not good at this mom thing. It’s not all day, but it pops up a few times.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Sometimes I’ll suddenly worry that the baby isn’t breathing right or that I missed something important, even when everyone says he looks fine. It’s quick—like a little jolt—and then I can calm myself down, but it keeps popping up out of nowhere a few times a day.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason
Not really panicky, no. I get those quick worries about the baby, but I haven’t had that full-blown scared or racing-heart feeling.
Things have been getting on top of me

Some days it feels like the to-do list never ends—feeding, laundry, trying to shower—and I’ll think, “How am I going to get through all this?” I manage, but it can feel a bit overwhelming for a little while.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

No, I’m still sleeping pretty well once I get the chance. Sometimes it takes me a little while to fall asleep because my mind keeps running through baby stuff, but I wouldn’t say I’m so unhappy that it keeps me awake.
I have felt sad or miserable

I do feel sad or kind of flat a few days a week—like yesterday I just sat on the couch and cried for a minute when the baby wouldn’t nap—but it usually passes after a little while. I wouldn’t call it miserable all the time, more like down or blue off and on.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying
Yeah, that’s happened—maybe once or twice this past week. It’s usually when I’m already tired and the baby’s fussy; I’ll just tear up for a bit, feel better after a good cry, and then keep going.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me
No, never. I’ve felt tired or discouraged, but I’ve never thought about hurting myself.

stats.query:
postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 12: Postpartum Depression / Anxiety Screening Note  
Date: [today]

Presenting symptoms endorsed:
- Dysthymic mood most days, with tearfulness 1–2×/week  
- Marked reduction in anticipatory pleasure ("I guess that'll be nice")  
- Intermittent, self-critical guilt when infant is fussy  
- Brief, repetitive, unprovoked worries about infant safety; no panic attacks  
- Episodic sense of being overwhelmed by daily tasks; resolves with effort  
- No sleep-onset problems related to mood; occasional delay due to "mind racing"  
- No self-harm ideation

Pattern: Sub-threshold depressive features + situational anxiety; functional but distressed.

Screening significance:
- Possible minor-moderate postpartum depressive symptoms (EPDS items 2, 8, 9)  
- Postpartum anxiety features without panic (EPDS items 4, 6)

Risk factors present: Low mood, anhedonia, guilt, transient crying spells, intrusive worries. No safety concerns identified.

Summary: Patient reports fluctuating low mood, diminished enjoyment, self-blame, and recurrent baby-focused worries beginning since delivery; retains basic functioning, denies suicidal ideation. Findings warrant continued monitoring, psycho-education, and consideration of formal EPDS/PHQ-9 for baseline score.
